messages:
maria: Quick sync — thinking of proposing a lightweight "runtime-auth-shim" for Private/Dedicated. It would sit in front of the inference runtime and mint short-lived per-request service tokens that carry org/project claims. Pros: reduces changes to downstream services, centralizes rotation. Cons: added hop & complexity, harder audit traces. Thoughts?

ajay: +1 for centralizing rotation. How does this interact with existing per-route RBAC? We'd still need ability to override claims coming from customer-managed control plane.

lucas: Concerned about latency; adding shim could add 5–20ms tail. Can we batch mints / reuse ephemeral tokens per connection?

maria: Good points. Implementation idea: shim issues JWTs with 1–5m TTL and embeds "orig_request_id" claim for traceability. Runtime caches them keyed by (caller, route, model, ip) for reuse for TTL window.

kai: Reuse window seems ok. But auditability: who queries the token store? Need to push all issuance events to audit log stream. Also ensure tokens include non-replay nonce.

ajay: For private installs we can't assume central KMS. Shim should support customer KMS/HSM signing, plus a fallback to local ephemeral key for dev mode.

maria: Agree. Also thinking about a "passthrough" mode: if upstream provides a bound token (e.g., org-scoped API key), shim validates and forwards claims without minting. That keeps latency minimal.

lucas: How do we prevent claim escalation if shim accepts upstream token? Need strict validation: only accept tokens signed by known roots and map allowed claim subsets per config.

maria: Exactly. We'll define a per-tenant policy: allowed claim elevation list, allowed routes, and token acceptance policy (mint-only, passthrough-allowlist).

deploy-bot: deploy status: canary image pushed: docker.redwood/runtime-auth-shim:pr-482 — logs show initialization ok on staging.

kai: Ops question: who owns rotation ops? Suggest SRE + customer ops for Private. Also alerting on failed sign attempts.

ajay: UX: SDK behavior — if shim mints 401->refresh flow? Better if shim does all retry so SDKs see only 200/429/500, not auth churn.

maria: Good. I'll draft RFC with: design, threat model, perf budget (p95 tail < 10ms added), configs (acceptance, caching), KMS integration surface, telemetry hooks. Putting draft into rfc/auth/runtime-shim.md.

lucas: One more: open models and hosted mode — do we need shim there? Hosted already has token service. Maybe share code but enable "shim-as-library" to embed into runtime when running in-proc.

kai: Nice. For Private on-prem installs, include a migration plan: start in passthrough dev mode, then enable minting once policies validated.

maria: Thanks. If no objections I'll post RFC later today and tag @security-review and @sre.

ajay: :thumbsup:
